jobs.title: EHS Manager
jobs.description:
About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

Position Overview

The EHS Manager will lead the Environmental, Health & Safety programs and activities for AMP-2 manufacturing operations in KAEC. The role is responsible for establishing and maintaining a strong EHS culture while ensuring regulatory compliance, effective risk management, and safe execution of manufacturing activities.

The EHS Manager will partner closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Facilities, Logistics, Maintenance, HR, and other functions to identify and mitigate workplace risks and integrate EHS requirements into day-to-day operations, new equipment installations, production ramp-up, and continuous improvement activities.

Internal AMP-2 planning confirms dedicated EHS support across General Assembly, Manufacturing/Logistics, Paint and BIW.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead the implementation and continuous improvement of the site EHS Management System.

• Ensure compliance with applicable Saudi Arabian environmental, occupational health and safety, civil defense, and industrial regulatory requirements, as well as company EHS standards.

• Provide EHS leadership and direction across AMP-2 manufacturing operations, including General Assembly, Body-in-White, Paint, Stamping, Logistics, Facilities, Maintenance, and supporting functions.

• Lead workplace hazard identification, risk assessments, Job Safety Analysis (JSA), inspections, and EHS audits.

• Develop and implement corrective and preventive actions to eliminate or reduce workplace risks.

• Lead investigations of injuries, incidents, near misses, environmental events, and high-risk conditions, including root-cause analysis and corrective action tracking.

• Establish and monitor site EHS KPIs, leading and lagging indicators, and management reporting.

• Partner with Engineering and Manufacturing teams during equipment installation, commissioning, process changes, and production ramp-up to ensure EHS requirements are incorporated from the design stage.

• Drive contractor safety programs and ensure contractors comply with site EHS requirements.

• Oversee programs related to LOTO, machine safety, confined spaces, working at height, electrical safety, chemical safety, ergonomics, material handling, PPE, and permit-to-work systems.

• Support environmental compliance programs covering waste management, hazardous materials, emissions, spill prevention, and environmental controls.

• Partner with Emergency Response and site stakeholders to maintain effective emergency preparedness and response programs.

• Lead EHS communication, training, awareness campaigns, toolbox talks, and leadership engagement initiatives.

• Coach managers and supervisors on their EHS responsibilities and promote a culture where safety ownership is embedded within operations.

• Support occupational health and industrial hygiene programs, including exposure assessments and ergonomic risk management.

• Conduct regular management reviews and communicate significant risks, trends, and improvement opportunities to site leadership.

• Support implementation and maintenance of ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 management systems.

The internal AMP-2 ergonomics JD specifically references ISO 45001 and ISO 14001, manufacturing risk management, equipment commissioning, production ramp-up, KPIs, audits, occupational health, and collaboration with Production, Manufacturing Engineering, Facilities, Logistics and Industrial Engineering, which I have carried into this manager-level scope.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Engineering, Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related discipline.

• Typically 8+ years of progressive EHS experience, preferably within automotive, manufacturing, industrial, or similarly complex operations.

• Previous experience in an EHS leadership or management role within a manufacturing environment.

• Strong knowledge of occupational safety, environmental compliance, risk management, and incident investigation.

• Strong understanding of manufacturing processes and associated EHS risks.

• Experience supporting new facility launches, equipment commissioning, or manufacturing ramp-up is highly desirable.

• Strong leadership, communication, influencing, and stakeholder-management skills.

• Ability to work effectively across Engineering, Manufacturing, Facilities, Logistics, HR, and senior leadership.

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret EHS data, identify trends, and drive corrective actions.

• Fluent professional English required; Arabic is an advantage.

Preferred Certifications

• NEBOSH International General Certificate or Diploma

• ISO 45001 Lead Auditor

• ISO 14001 Lead Auditor

• Certified Safety Professional (CSP) or equivalent

• Relevant Saudi EHS, industrial safety, or environmental certifications

The internal AMP-2 EHS material also identifies NEBOSH IGC and ISO 45001 Lead Auditor as preferred qualifications for EHS-related specialist roles.

Preferred Experience

• Automotive or high-volume manufacturing experience.

• Experience with new factory launches and production ramp-up.

• Experience managing EHS programs across multiple manufacturing shops or operational areas.

• Knowledge of robotics, automation, machine guarding, manufacturing equipment, and material handling systems.

• Experience working with government agencies and regulatory authorities in Saudi Arabia.

• Strong experience in incident investigation, root-cause analysis, auditing, and corrective-action management.

Compensation & Benefits: Lucid offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance; life and disability coverage; paid time off; paid holidays, paid sick leave; and a 401(k) retirement plan. Hourly/non-exempt employees accrue up to 120 hours paid time off, and salaried/exempt employee accrue up to 160 hours paid time off.  Eligible employees may also participate in Lucid’s equity program and/or a discretionary annual cash incentive program. Incentive and equity awards, if applicable, are determined based on individual performance, role scope, market considerations, and overall company results, in accordance with the terms of the applicable plans.

Equal Opportunity: At Lucid, we believe diversity strengthens everything we build. Lucid Motors is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing an inclusive workplace for all. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, national or ethnic origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable state or federal laws and regulations.

Accessibility: Lucid Motors is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need any accommodation to participate in the application process, please contact us at TA-Operations <@> lucidmotors.com. This email address is designated solely for accommodation requests and is not monitored for job applications or resume submissions. To be considered for employment, all applications must be submitted through the Lucid Motors Careers website.

Candidate Data Privacy: By submitting your application, you understand and agree that your personal data will be processed in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Notice.

About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

Position Overview

An Ergonomics Specialist will lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of ergonomics programs across manufacturing, warehouse, logistics, office, and construction support activities. The successful candidate will be responsible for identifying and mitigating musculoskeletal disorder (MSD) risks, improving workstation design, supporting operational readiness activities, and driving ergonomic excellence through engineering controls, employee engagement, and data-driven improvements.

Key Responsibilities

•    Develop, implement, and continuously improve the site Ergonomics Management Program.
•    Conduct ergonomic assessments of manufacturing workstations, warehouse activities, logistics operations, maintenance tasks, and office environments.
•    Evaluate tasks using recognized ergonomic assessment tools such as RULA, REBA, the NIOSH Lifting Equation, Liberty Mutual Tables, Snook Tables, and OCRA.
•    Identify ergonomic risk factors including repetitive motion, awkward postures, excessive force, contact stress, vibration exposure, and manual material handling activities.
•    Lead ergonomic reviews during equipment design, process development, line modifications, and operational readiness activities.
•    Collaborate with Production, Manufacturing Engineering, Facilities, Logistics, and Industrial Engineering teams to integrate ergonomic principles into workplace design.
•    Recommend and validate engineering controls to eliminate or reduce ergonomic risks.
•    Participate in new equipment commissioning and ensure ergonomic requirements are incorporated into machine and workstation designs.
•    Conduct workstation validations and support production ramp-up activities.
•    Analyze injury, discomfort, and first aid data to identify trends and improvement opportunities.
•    Lead investigations related to musculoskeletal injuries and develop corrective actions.
•    Develop ergonomic standards, guidelines, and design specifications for manufacturing operations.
•    Support continuous improvement initiatives to enhance productivity, quality, and employee well-being.
•    Deliver ergonomic awareness training and coaching for employees, supervisors, engineers, and leadership teams.
•    Support industrial hygiene and occupational health programs where ergonomic risks intersect with worker health.
•    Establish key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure program effectiveness and risk reduction.
•    Conduct periodic ergonomic audits and workplace inspections.
•    Work closely with medical providers, occupational health personnel, and Human Resources regarding return-to-work and accommodation assessments.
•    Support ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 management system requirements related to workplace risk management and continuous improvement.
•    Prepare reports, presentations, and business cases supporting ergonomic improvement projects.

Preferred Certifications:
•    Certified Professional Ergonomist (CPE)
•    Board Certified Professional Ergonomist (BCPE)
•    Certified Business Ergonomics Specialist (CBES)
•    NEBOSH International General Certificate (IGC)
•    ISO 45001 Lead Auditor
o    Required Knowledge & Skills:
•    Strong understanding of ergonomics and human factors engineering principles.
•    Knowledge of occupational health regulations and international ergonomic standards.
•    Experience with ergonomic risk assessment methodologies and tools.
•    Ability to interpret injury data and perform trend analysis.
•    Strong project management and problem-solving skills.
•    Experience working with manufacturing equipment, assembly processes, and material handling systems.
•    Proficiency in Microsoft Office and data analysis tools.
•    Excellent communication and presentation skills in English; Arabic is preferred.
•    Ability to influence stakeholders and drive cross-functional collaboration.
•    Strong analytical mindset and commitment to continuous improvement.
•    Experience performing ergonomic assessments in high-volume production environments.
•    Experience supporting workstation design and process optimization projects.
o    Preferred Experience:
•    Automotive manufacturing experience.
•    Experience supporting new factory launches or production ramp-up activities.
•    Experience with wearable technology, motion capture systems, or digital ergonomics software.
•    Experience in lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.
•    Knowledge of robotics, automation, and human-machine interface design.

Minimum Qualifications

•    Minimum of 4 years of experience in industrial ergonomics within manufacturing, automotive, logistics, warehousing, or heavy industrial environments.

jobs.title: Head of Sales
jobs.description:
HEAD OF SALES, NEW YORK



Job title: Head of Sales, New York

Department: Sales

Reports to: Chief Revenue Officer

Location: New York, NY (in office)





ABOUT FUNDWELL

Fundwell helps small and medium-sized businesses access capital with greater clarity, speed and confidence. Our platform brings financing options and experienced specialists together, helping business owners compare offers, understand their choices and move from application to funding through a streamlined process.




YOUR ROLE AT FUNDWELL


Fundwell is building a modern, data-driven inside sales organization, and we’re looking for an energetic sales leader to run our New York sales floor.

This is a tactical and strategic role for someone who thrives alongside reps: running huddles, reviewing pipelines, listening to calls, coaching live deals, and holding the team accountable. You will hire and develop reps, guide them through ramp, and build the daily habits that produce consistent performance serving small business owners.

You will own the floor’s results, people, and operating rhythm, partnering closely with Enablement, Operations, and HR to establish clear expectations, strengthen coaching, and make high performance part of how the team works every day.

Balancing hands-on execution with strategic leadership, you will partner with the Chief Revenue Officer and executive team to translate company growth objectives into a scalable sales strategy, capacity plans, and measurable revenue commitments. You will use insights from the floor to shape decisions on sales structure, talent investment, and productivity, building the leadership bench and operating model needed to sustain long-term growth.




HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT




Lead a structured, high-energy sales floor

 - Lead a team built on clearly defined roles (openers or SDRs, closers or account executives, and retention reps), each with a narrow, measurable scope.

 - Bring our base-plus-variable compensation plan to life on the floor, so every rep knows the activities and behaviors that drive their earnings.

 - Set clear expectations for every role, so reps know what good looks like each day, week and month.

Build a high-performing, data-driven sales floor

 - Run the floor on data: activities, connect and conversion rates, pipeline, approvals and funded volume, using the sales scorecard, Salesforce, Five9 and call recordings.

 - Set daily and weekly targets, track them on a set cadence and act early when a rep or the team is off pace.

 - Build forecasting discipline so leadership can predict monthly results before the month begins.

 - Partner with Operations and Technology on lead flow, deal routing and the tools that make reps more productive, including AI call scoring and automation.

Coach every rep from hire through success tiers

 - Own the rep lifecycle: hiring, onboarding and ramp, development, and promotion through clear performance tiers.

 - Partner with the Head of Enablement to deliver the Fundwell Academy in New York, from new-hire ramp to ongoing skill building.

 - Coach daily through call reviews, ride-alongs, role-play and one-on-ones, so improvement is measurable and specific.

 - Address underperformance quickly and fairly, with clear plans and support from HR.

Hire and build the team

 - Build a steady recruiting pipeline for sales talent with HR, and hire against Fundwell’s competencies.

 - Develop team leads and future managers, so the team can grow without losing quality.

Protect the customer and the business

 - Make sure every rep recommends the financing that fits the business owner, and explains cost and terms plainly before they sign.

 - Uphold compliance standards for merchant data, credit pulls, opt-outs and funder requirements.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Team: a motivated, fully staffed New York floor where every rep knows their role, their numbers and how to win.

 - Performance: a rising share of ramped reps consistently hit their targets, in line with the company goal of moving from x % to y%.

 - Predictability: monthly results are forecast accurately before the month begins.

 - Ramp: new hires reach productivity faster, with clear milestones through each success tier.

 - Bench: a hiring pipeline and developing team leads let the floor grow on plan.

 - Customer outcomes: conversion and renewal rates improve, and deals fit the business owner’s needs.


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 10+ years of sales experience, including 5+ years managing and coaching an inside sales team.

 - Required: experience in high-volume, transactional sales to small and medium-sized businesses in lending, merchant cash advance, revenue-based financing and/or payments.

 - Experience building or scaling a structured inside sales team, with defined roles and activity-based compensation.

 - Deep comfort with sales data: dashboards, conversion funnels, activity metrics and forecasting. Experience with Salesforce and a dialer such as Five9.

 - Proven coaching ability: you have built onboarding and ramp programs and moved average performers into top performers.

 - Experience hiring at volume and building tiered career paths for sales reps.

 - Strong ethics and judgment in selling financial products to business owners.

 - A visible, energetic leadership style on the floor: you set the pace, celebrate wins and hold people to a high bar.
   


WHY FUNDWELL?

 - Real ownership: build and lead the New York sales floor, with leadership backing and the tools to win.

 - Join a growing fintech investing in data, AI and modern sales tools, including live dashboards and AI call scoring.

 - Work in person with a New York team that moves fast and cares about doing right by small businesses.
   


OUR COMMITMENT TO YOU

Fundwell is an equal employment opportunity employer. We make employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Bot Detection Researcher (EST)
jobs.description:
The Research team at HUMAN is eager to protect the internet, and is passionate about innovating  and winning against our attackers. As the ‘mind’ behind our products, we demand ourselves to bring our best and never stop learning attitude, eventually making our products’ trillions decisions per day as accurate as possible.

Our group includes data scientists and  security researchers, working together towards reaching our goals and for mutual personal development. We’re currently looking for a talented data security researcher to join our team!



What you'll do:

 - Research and implement innovative ways to identify and block malicious activity.

 - Work closely with our development, Product and incident response teams.

 - Deal with huge amounts of data and use various tools to find solutions to complex problems.

 - Take part in a global core team in the company, made up of researchers and data scientists, and as such - you will have many opportunities to initiate and impact.
   
   

Who you are:

 - 3+ years of experience with data tools and platforms (SQL, Pandas, Kibana etc.).

 - A researcher mindset - knowledge in research methods and how to conduct a profound research.

 - A proven record of solving problems using data manipulation.

 - Deep knowledge and understanding on how the internet works.

 - Familiarity with the cyber and attack world, application level  attacks is a plus.

 - Great motivation to invest in learning and development, as well as a desire to influence and constantly improve.

 - A strong sense of ownership which drives you to find ways to do things better, faster, and reduce costs.

 - A great team player - open, transparent and happy to work in close collaboration with other stakeholders.

 - Constantly drive for correctness and performance, in that order.
   
   

About HUMAN Security



HUMAN was founded in a Brooklyn sci-fi bookstore with a hacker mindset and the lofty mission of making the internet safer by putting humans first. Today, our Human Defense Platform safeguards enterprises from sophisticated bots, fraud, and account abuse, verifying the humanity of more than 20 trillion interactions per week for the world’s biggest brands and internet platforms.



HUMAN is an equal opportunity workplace dedicated to protecting the internet's integrity for everyone. We believe in putting people first, embracing diversity of thought from our global teams, and welcoming all individuals to share their unique experiences as we fight cybercrime together. We support our Humans with a comprehensive total rewards package for personal and professional development, including well-being and learning stipends, flexible work options, and dedicated time off. While our HQ is in NYC, we have teams worldwide.



HUMAN is growing fast, and there’s never been a more meaningful time to join us. If you thrive on solving complex problems and want to help shape the future of cybersecurity, join us as we build a safer, more human internet.



If you are an individual with a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please contact us directly.

jobs.title: Seasonal Waiting Staff - Food and Beverage Assistant
jobs.description:
Seasonal Waiting Staff - Food and Beverage Assistant

Please only apply if you have a year of experience in a Hotel, Events Venue, Restaurant or Bar.

We do not have any opportunities for sponsorship, so please only apply if you have unrestricted right to work in the United Kingdom.

Alcohol service is a must, so please only apply if you are over the age of 18-years.

We are seeking dedicated and enthusiastic Waiting Staff to join our vibrant team in a fast-paced Full-Service Hotel environment. As Waiting Staff, you will play a crucial role in providing exceptional customer service, ensuring that our guests have a memorable festive experience. Your responsibilities will encompass customer service, face to face interactions, serving food as part of the banquet service team, bar service, and maintaining a clean and organised front-of-house and back-of-house.

You are an ambassador for the exceptional service and cuisine that are hallmarks of our food & beverage experience. Your warm, personal attention and knowledge of our outstanding offerings makes guests feel unique and valued.

All applicants must be able to demonstrate fast adaptiveness as working between Bar, food service. Clearing on the floor including food, waste, and glass collections which will be a daily challenge for the team. Event shifts will run from 5 PM to 2 AM. Christmas Day and New Years' Eve are working requirements for this role.

What you will be doing:

• Greet and seat guests promptly upon arrival, providing a warm welcome and information about the event and running order.
• Assist guests regarding menu items in an informative and helpful way
• Follow the 5 / 10 Rule for all guest encounters.
• Take accurate drink orders using the Zonal POS system.

• Maintain cleanliness of tables, function rooms and service stations throughout the shift.
• Collaborate with kitchen staff to ensure smooth communication regarding orders and special requests.
• Handle guest inquiries and complaints professionally, striving for resolution to ensure satisfaction and elevating to leadership team where required.

Your experience and skills include:

• Ability to focus attention on guest needs, remaining calm and courteous at all times
• Ability to work well under pressure in a fast paced environment
• Strong understanding of food safety practices to maintain a safe dining environment.
• Basic maths skills for handling transactions accurately and efficiently.
• Experience in a bar or hospitality setting is advantageous but not essential.
• Excellent time management skills to balance multiple tasks during peak service times.
• Ability to work collaboratively within a team while also being self-motivated when required.
• Take immense pride in the hotel and service standards so the very best can be experienced by our guests.
• Knowledge of cocktails is beneficial for assisting in bar tasks.
• Strong communication skills to engage with guests effectively and provide outstanding service.
• Strength and manual handling of function room furniture to rearrange quickly and comfortably

Your team and working environment:

• Meal on shift when working 8-hours
• Free on-site parking
• Gym membership at times agreed with the Leisure Manager
• Discounts on hotel services including Spa treatments, food, drink, and Golf
• Employee benefit card offering discounted rates in Accor worldwide for you and your family
• Learning programs through our Academies designed to sharpen your skills
• Ability to make a difference through our Corporate Social Responsibility activities, like Planet 21
• Career development opportunities with national and international promotion opportunities. The sky is your limit

Our commitment to Diversity & Inclusion:

We are an inclusive company and our ambition is to attract, recruit and promote diverse talent.

jobs.title: Senior Python Engineer
jobs.description:
At D-Fend Solutions, our people are our greatest strength — and technology is our passion. Our team of innovators and subject matter experts, including veterans of elite military intelligence technology units, is transforming the way organizations protect themselves from drone threats.

As the global leader in cyber-takeover counter-drone technology, we design and deliver advanced, software-defined solutions that empower our customers to detect, take control, and safely land unauthorized drones — with precision and reliability.

Every day, we push the boundaries of innovation to meet real-world security challenges across industries and environments. We’re proud of our cutting-edge technology, our global reach, and the impact we make in securing the skies.

We’re seeking passionate professionals who thrive in a fast-paced, creative, and collaborative environment — those who want to be part of the next generation of airspace security innovation.

Join D-Fend Solutions and help make the world a safer place.
Become a D-Fender! Work with the world’s leading cyber-takeover counter-drone technology provider and shape the future of safe airspace.


Scope:
As a Senior Python Engineer, you will play a key role in the development of our cutting-edge solutions to detect, track and mitigate drones.
 
Your primary responsibility will be to successfully implement real-time, multi-core, and multi-threaded software tasks and continuously develop new features and capabilities for an up-to-date response to new drone models and components, while collaborating  with our algorithms and radio-frequency (RF) engineers. 
 
This includes coding over a Linux platform, primarily in user space, with a rich and fully automated Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) platform. In addition, you will implement Scrum and Agile methodologies in your tasks, while taking features from the early requirement stage through design, implementation, integration, and then handing it over  to our validation team.

jobs.title: Manager, Customer Experience
jobs.description:
CareDx, Inc. is a leading precision medicine solutions company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of clinically differentiated, high-value healthcare solutions for transplant patients and caregivers. CareDx offers products, testing services, and digital healthcare solutions along the pre- and post-transplant patient journey, and is the leading provider of genomics-based information for transplant patients.

Reporting to the Director of Customer Experience, the Manager, Customer Experience – AlloHeme is responsible for leading the Clinical Liaison team supporting the CareDx Cellular Therapy & Transplant Portfolio. This role provides clinical, operational, and strategic leadership to ensure exceptional support for healthcare professionals and patients throughout their experience with CareDx.

The Manager will lead and develop a high performing field-based Clinical Liaison team while also directly engaging with Cellular Therapy and Transplant customers in the field. The Manager will build trusted customer relationships, provide clinical education, support testing workflows, and drive successful adoption and utilization of Cell Therapy solutions, while coaching and developing the Clinical Liaison team.

This role will use data and analytics to evaluate ordering trends, account activity, adoption, workflow opportunities, and team performance. The Manager will partner closely with Commercial Leadership, Laboratory Operations, Reimbursement, Medical Affairs and other cross-functional teams to identify opportunities, resolve complex customer needs, improve processes, and enhance the overall healthcare provider and patient experience.

Successful candidates will be experienced clinical leaders who are highly organized, analytical, collaborative, and comfortable leading teams in a fast-paced environment while advancing patient care across Cellular Therapy and Transplantation.

Responsibilities:

• Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing Clinical Liaison team supporting Cellular Therapy and Transplantation (CTT) centers.

• Maintain direct field based customer responsibilities, engaging with priority CTT centers to build trusted relationships, provide clinical education, support testing workflows, and drive adoption and utilization of CareDx solutions.

• Provide regular field coaching using the PACE coaching model to assess Clinical Liaison competencies, provide actionable feedback, and support continued development.

• Provide clinical and operational oversight of customer onboarding, education, testing workflows, account support, and resolution of complex customer needs.

• Establish consistent Clinical Liaison practices and coach the team on account planning, customer engagement, clinical education, territory prioritization, and effective use of CareDx tools and resources.

• Analyze ordering trends, account activity, customer engagement, and team performance to identify opportunities for increased adoption, targeted education, workflow improvement, and field support.

• Establish and monitor team goals and key performance indicators, using data and business insights to identify gaps, prioritize opportunities, and develop action plans.

jobs.title: RVP, Solutions Engineering, Enterprise
jobs.description:
ABOUT FACTORY



Our mission is to create a world where software builds and improves itself.

We build the platform for self-improving software development, helping the world's largest enterprise engineering teams turn their organizations into autonomous software factories. Customers including Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile run Factory to ship code, review PRs, run tests, and deploy continuously - getting smarter with every cycle.

In 2026, we raised $200M at a $5B valuation, bringing our total funding to over $400M. We are backed by world-class investors and operators including Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Blackstone, Ali Ghodsi (CEO of Databricks), and Frank Slootman (Former CEO of Snowflake).




ABOUT THE ROLE

Factory is hiring a Regional Vice President to build out and lead Enterprise Solutions Engineering across the Western US. Our Enterprise Solutions Engineers own the full customer lifecycle, pre-sales and post-sales: discovery, demos, proofs of concept, security and architecture reviews, pilot delivery, and the ongoing adoption and expansion of Factory once a customer is live. This is a second-line management role: you will hire and develop the managers who lead the region's SE teams, hire Solutions Engineers with them, and own the technical win and the production outcome for our Enterprise accounts in the region.

You will set the strategy, hiring plan, and operating rhythm for Enterprise Solutions Engineering in the West, and plan the region's growth with Enterprise Sales leadership at the VP level. You will work closely with Product and Engineering. This role suits someone who has managed multiple teams, knows how developers build software, and makes sound calls under deal pressure.



WHAT YOU WILL DO AND ACHIEVE

 - Build out the West region: hire and develop the managers who lead the region's SE teams, hire Solutions Engineers with them, and give each team clear goals and performance standards

 - Develop your managers as leaders: coach them on hiring, deal reviews, and performance conversations, and build a bench of future leaders in the region

 - Plan capacity with Enterprise Sales leadership several quarters ahead, and tie SE hiring and coverage to the region's pipeline and forecast

 - Set the operating rhythm across the region's teams: one playbook for discovery, pilot scoping, success metrics, security and compliance reviews, production rollout, and ongoing adoption and expansion, with a regular review of each team against it

 - Turn what the teams learn in the field into repeatable plays and evaluation standards that every SE in the region uses

 - Own technical win rate, time-to-technical-win, coverage of the region's largest deals, pilot-to-production conversion, and post-sales adoption and expansion across the region; report them to GTM leadership and use them to coach the managers

 - Build relationships with the engineering and security leaders of the region's largest customers, and guide the largest deals, escalations, and rollouts with your managers

 - Turn patterns from across the region into clear priorities for Product and Engineering leadership, and keep the teams current on competitors and the market

 - Make agentic development, with Factory first, part of how the region's SE teams prepare, demo, and run evaluations


QUALIFICATIONS

You do not need to meet every requirement to be a strong candidate. If you have related experience, we encourage you to apply.

 - 8-10 years of management experience, managing multiple teams and building out a region, including leading managers who run SE teams, in Enterprise Solutions Engineering, Field Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or customer engineering in enterprise software, spanning pre-sales and post-sales

 - A strong record of hiring and developing leaders: you know how to source, assess, and close managers and Solutions Engineers, coach first-line leaders, and handle hard performance situations

 - Technical credibility in modern software development, developer tooling, CI/CD, and AI coding tools, and you can test a complex architecture before a customer commits to it

 - Operational discipline: you run multiple teams on technical win rates and pilot outcomes, and you plan several quarters ahead with Sales while you keep weekly execution on track

 - A record of tying team design and hiring to revenue results, and you can show those results in numbers

 - You influence senior leaders in Product, Engineering, and Sales, and you keep technical answers honest when a deal is under pressure

 - You advise customer executives on complex rollouts and critical escalations, and you can turn around a stalled evaluation anywhere in the region

 - Strong written and spoken communication, from a pilot review with engineers to a planning session with executives


NICE TO HAVE

 - Hands-on use of agentic coding tools, and experience selling LLM-based products or developer platforms

 - Background as a software engineer or in a technical consulting role

 - Experience building out a new region or function for a high-growth company

 - Experience with a structured enterprise sales methodology, for example MEDDICC

jobs.title: Product Manager, Network & Accounts
jobs.description:
PRODUCT MANAGER; NETWORK & ACCOUNTS

Location: Remote - United Kingdom United States, and Europe (France, Germany, Portugal)




ABOUT WORLDLY

Worldly is the world’s most comprehensive impact intelligence platform — delivering real data to businesses on impacts within their supply chain. Worldly is trusted by 40,000 global brands, retailers, and manufacturers to provide the single source of ESG intelligence they need to accelerate business and industry transformation.

Through strategic and meaningful customer relationships, Worldly provides key insights around supplier performance, product impact, trends analysis, and compliance. When a company wants to change how business is done, we enable that systemic shift.

Backed by a dedicated global team of individuals aligned by values, Worldly proudly operates as a public benefit corporation with backing from mission-aligned investors. Want to learn more? Read our story http://worldly.io/about.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Worldly's Network connects the brands and retailers who source goods, the suppliers who make them, and the verifiers who confirm the accuracy of supplier assessments. Brands use it to find and connect with their suppliers, and suppliers join to share assessments with the brands they work with. Every Worldly product, including the Higg Index, depends on the Network being accurate, because an assessment is only useful when it's attached to the right facility and visible to the right brand. The Network is also the foundation of Worldly's transparency and traceability work: a brand can only trace what it sources if every supplier and facility in the chain appears in the Network once, correctly.

This is a technical product role with a customer problem at the center of it. You will own the experiences that bring customers into the Network and keep them there:

 - Getting in: finding a company or facility, joining or claiming it for their Worldly account, and resolving duplicates and conflicting claims so each real-world entity has one trusted record.

 - Buying in: purchase, checkout and subscriptions.

 - Managing: accounts, users and access once a customer is in.

You will spend real time with brands, sourcing teams, suppliers, and our internal Customer Success teams to understand where these experiences help them achieve their goals and where they fall short, and you will set the measures that show whether they're improving.

You'll collaborate with product managers across Platform and Traceability, turning what customers need into clear requirements for the shared services behind the Network.





WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Align teams and cross-functional partners so everyone understands what is being built (and why)

 - Translate product vision into initiatives, epics and stories

 - Run discovery with brands, suppliers, and Customer Success on how the Network is used; set and track KPIs

 - Cultivate backlog prioritization for your areas of focus

 - Write clear specs and plain-language definitions that engineers, CS, and customers can all use; support release planning and change management.





WE'D LIKE TO SEE

 - 5+ years of product management experience on technical or platform products

 - You can reason about data as a graph: entities, identifiers, and relationships. You have shipped onboarding, identity or account experiences where users must find, claim or de-duplicate records, and you know what it takes for a customer to trust a record

 - Comfortable reading data models and API contracts well enough to write precise requirements for platform teams and judge the trade-offs they propose

 - Deep customer focus: you spend time with the people who build and use supplier networks, you can explain a technical concept to a sourcing manager in plain language, and you decide from what customers do, not only what they say

 - Strong analytical skills; you define conversion, adoption and data quality metrics for the experiences you own and use them to prioritize




IT HELPS IF YOU HAVE

 - Experience with entity resolution, de-duplication or master data products

 - Experience in apparel, footwear, or consumer goods supply chains: how brands source, who sits at each tier, and what brands and suppliers each need from a shared platform

 - Exposure to sustainability data such as the Higg Index, or to supplier registries and third-party entity data.




WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOU

 - Comprehensive benefits offerings. 90% employee premium and 75% spouse/dependent premium covered by Worldly.

 - Company-sponsored 401k with up to 4% match.

 - Incentive Stock Options

 - 100% Parental Paid Leave

 - Unlimited PTO

 - 13 company holidays




LIFE AT WORLDLY

Our team is motivated to transform the way products are made. By helping our customers succeed in a new era of sustainable production, we are able to build technology that makes a difference on a planetary level.

Our team represents over 15 countries, and brings unique experiences from technology to farming to the table. Surround yourself with kind, enthusiastic, and dedicated people who put collaboration and growth at the center of our shared goals.

Benefits and Perks

 - Earn a competitive salary and performance-based bonuses. Get healthcare, retirement matching, and equity for US employees.

 - Use the office stipend to get the supplies you need. Combat zoom fatigue with no-meeting Fridays.

 - Flexible time off. Take the time you need to recharge. Our culture encourages team members to explore and rest to be their best selves.

 - We're remote, not lonely. Join the culture committee, coffee chats, or a variety of other interest groups.




TRAVEL NOTICE

Roles at Worldly may require occasional travel to support business needs, including but not limited to team collaboration, customer engagement, or company events.




EQUITY STATEMENT

We believe it’s essential to reflect the diversity of those we strive to serve. True innovation happens when everyone has room at the table, including the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel. We’re dedicated to building a culturally and experientially diverse team that leads and works with empathy and respect.




COMPENSATION INFORMATION

Annual Base Salary:

 - €86,000 - €105,000 Annually (EU/UK Range)

 - $120,000 -$135,000 USD Annually (US Range)

10% Annual Bonus Potential

Incentive Stock Option Package (for approved countries)

Work-From-Home Stipends

*Final compensation figures will be determined based on a wide variety of factors, including experience and location. These factors will be evaluated and considered by Worldly throughout the entirety of this process.

**For candidates located outside the U.S., the salary range listed in USD will be paid in the local currency equivalent at the time of offer using the then-current exchange rate.

jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineer (Starlink)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

FULL STACK SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK)

At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.

As a Full Stack Engineer, you will work closely with a mix of both external customers and internal partners across all engineering disciplines here at SpaceX to bring observability to a rapidly expanding network of millions of assets. The tools and applications you build will empower Starlink customers to manage their deployed assets in aviation, maritime, and enterprise environments while also bringing enhanced development to key features across various internal and external platforms. On this team, we will rely on you to be a key figure in the successful development of mission critical, high performance web applications. Our full stack engineers can work on a variety of sub teams, a few of which are included below:

• Internal Tooling & Development

• Web Application Development

• Consumer Platform Development

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Develop well-architected, responsive, and performant web applications

• Develop highly reliable and available software systems for Starlink

• Design and implement highly available, fault-tolerant networks that operates for long periods of time with minimal maintenance at scale

• Deliver expert level Typescript, HTML, and CSS code for modern browsers

• Full stack application development (our system is a .NET Core micro-service architecture running in Kubernetes with a React and Angular frontend)

• Craft aesthetically and functionally flawless user experiences

• Collaborate with peers on architecture, design, and code reviews

• Deep dive into your users’ problems to find and create efficient solutions

• Bring your voice to the table in team collaborations on architecture, design, and code reviews

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in a STEM discipline and 1+ years of software development experience (internship and/or project experience is acceptable); OR 3+ years of professional experience building full stack software in lieu of a degree

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Programming experience in Python, C#, .NET, Go, Scala, Java, or similar object-oriented language

• Production experience with Docker and Kubernetes

• Front-end experience in React, Angular, or similar JavaScript framework

• Database experience with PostgreSQL, SQL Server, or similar database technologies

• Experience with version control, continuous integration, and continuous delivery concepts.

• Expertise in profiling and improving application performance

• Experience with build systems (Make, Bazel/Pants/Buck, Gradle) and package management tools (pip, npm)

• Strong attention to detail

• Experience with UNIX-like operating systems and CI/CD tools

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 1: $150,000.00 - $175,000.00
Level 2: $175,000.00 - $210,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Performs unit-based reception, clerical, medical record and patient registration functions. Is capable of setting priorities and handling emergency situations in a calm manner. Is customer oriented and able to communicate with all levels of staff and patients and their families. Serves as liaison between patient care units and all other patient related departments. Manages the overall unit workflow in concert with the charge RN and/or assistant manager.

Responsibilities:

• Presents a friendly, approachable, professional demeanor and appearance.
• Provides accurate information and timely updates to patients and customers.
• Addresses questions and concerns promptly, or identifies appropriate person and resources to do so.
• Provides directions or help to patients and customers with finding their way.
• Uses effective service recovery skills to solve problems or service breakdowns when they occur.
• Demonstrates teamwork by helping co-workers within and across departments.
• Communicates effectively with others, respects diverse opinions and styles, acknowledges the assistance and contributions of others.
• Uses organizational and unit/department resources efficiently.
• Manages work schedule efficiently, completing tasks and assignments on time.
• Contributes to opportunities and processes for continuous improvement.
• Participates in efforts to reduce costs, streamline work processes, improve and grow services we provide.
• Communicates effectively and works cooperatively with other team members.
• Has respect for and understanding of other disciplines.
• Coordinates all work with the Manager and Charge Nurse.
• Communicates appropriately and clearly to Manager, Charge Nurse, co-workers and physicians.
• Consults other departments as appropriate to provide for an interdisciplinary approach to the patient's needs.
• Retrieves all lab results from computer and bring results to the attention of the nurse caring for the patient.
• Interacts professionally with patients/family and provides explanations and verbal reassurance as necessary.
• Prepares medical records for new admissions and disassembles the chart and forwards to Medical Records upon patient discharge.
• Maintains proper record assembly contents in chronological order behind tabs.
• Obtains necessary signatures and documents. Aware of Petition and Certificate process in regard to Involuntary Admissions.
• Transcribes accurately and clarifies handwritten, orders set physicians orders and clinical data. Enters and verifies orders in the computer to ensure timely and accurate delivery of medications, supplies, diagnostic/therapeutic tests/services.
• Seeks out and obtains learning opportunities.
• Participates in professional growth and development activities and shares knowledge from continuing education programs with co-workers.
• Demonstrates computer competence for order entry, results, documentation, policies, etc.
• Manages and operates equipment safety and correctly.
• Demonstrates the ability to be flexible, organized and function under stressful situations.
• Demonstrates confidence and success with multiple, high level, time sensitive tasks.
• Answers telephone, monitors unit closed circuit camera, and intercom/door entry system in a polite manner and communicates information to the appropriate staff/family.
• Utilizes critical thinking skills to successfully demonstrate the ability to prioritize and complete unit work quickly as the needs of the unit, patients, and staff change.
• Monitors patient's type in the computer against actual status and makes corrections when necessary.
• Performs pre-census and validates daily admission, discharge and census lists.
• Registers patient in the computer.
• Conducts telephone screenings (inquiry calls)in a fashion resulting in appropriate disposition based on the phone contact. Observes patient confidentiality rules and Release of Information data.
• Orders supplies and prints all forms used for patients charts.
• Performs other duties as assigned

Required:

• High School Diploma or GED equivalent
• Basic computer knowledge.
• Ability to communicate effectively in English, both verbal and in writing.
• Ability to assess and determine situations requiring an interpreter and to use interpreter services effectively
• Excellent customer service skills

Preferred:

• One year of experience in pertinent clinical specialty

jobs.title: Director, IT
jobs.description:
About Pantheon

Pantheon WebOps Platform powers the open web, running more than 300,000 sites in the cloud for customers including Google, Princeton, Salesloft and Doctors Without Borders. Every day, thousands of developers and marketers create, iterate, and scale WordPress and Drupal sites to reach billions of people globally. Pantheon’s multitenant, container-based platform enables organizations to manage all of their websites from a single dashboard. Organizations including Clorox and the United Nations drive results through accelerated development and real-time publishing using Pantheon’s collaborative workflows.

The Role

As the Director, IT, you will lead the strategic and operational management of Pantheon’s IT function, ensuring the delivery of secure, reliable, scalable, and employee-centered technology services.

This role is accountable for IT strategy, team leadership, service delivery, infrastructure, identity and endpoint operations, security controls, compliance readiness, vendor management, technology lifecycle management, and business continuity. You will lead the IT support and systems engineering function and partner closely with Business Systems, Information Security, Security Engineering, GRC, People, Legal, Finance, Engineering, and other cross-functional leaders.

You will establish an operating model that makes IT easy to engage, clear to own, and efficient to scale. You will turn recurring operational needs into durable processes, automation, documentation, and measurable services while serving as a senior escalation point for high-impact IT issues.

The role has global scope across Pantheon employees, contractors, offices, remote workers, endpoints, workplace technology, enterprise IT services, and internal IT operations.

What You'll Do

Strategic IT Leadership:

• Develop and execute Pantheon’s IT strategy, roadmap, and operating model, aligning technology initiatives with business objectives, employee needs, security requirements, and business continuity goals.

• Establish clear ownership, service boundaries, decision rights, escalation paths, and operating agreements across IT, Business Systems, Security, GRC, People, Legal, Finance, and Engineering.

• Translate business needs into sequenced programs, measurable outcomes, and clear tradeoffs for executive stakeholders.

• Identify and implement technologies, processes, and automation that improve operational efficiency, security, employee experience, and organizational scale.

Team Management:

• Lead, mentor, and develop the IT support and systems engineering team, fostering a culture of service excellence, technical ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

• Plan team capacity, coverage, hiring, succession, and skills development as Pantheon’s needs evolve.

• Allocate resources effectively across operational support, strategic programs, incidents, technical debt, and planned improvements.

• Establish expectations for documentation, service quality, operational discipline, and sustainable workload management.

• Partner with People and Finance on headcount planning, role design, performance management, and organizational development.

Infrastructure and Operations:

• Oversee the design, implementation, maintenance, and lifecycle management of IT systems, endpoints, networks, office technology, workplace platforms, and internal IT tooling.

• Own the IT-side strategy and operations for identity and access, endpoint management, device security, patching, software deployment, asset management, and hardware lifecycle processes.

• Ensure reliable operation of core workplace services, including identity, collaboration tools, endpoint platforms, office networks, conference-room technology, and employee hardware.

• Ensure onboarding, transfers, offboarding, access changes, device deployment, and equipment recovery are completed accurately, promptly, and auditable.

• Maintain accurate inventories of applications, licenses, devices, vendors, integrations, and business-critical dependencies.

IT Service Delivery and Automation:

• Own the internal IT service-management model, including intake, triage, incident response, request fulfillment, escalation, knowledge management, service reporting, and continual improvement.

• Establish and monitor service expectations and metrics such as response time, resolution time, employee satisfaction, backlog health, request quality, and automation rate.

• Improve the employee experience through clear support channels, reliable self-service, useful documentation, and consistent communications.

• Design scalable workflows for access requests, software provisioning, onboarding, offboarding, hardware tracking, and other repeatable employee requests.

• Use automation and integrations to reduce repetitive work, improve consistency, strengthen controls, and scale service delivery while preserving human escalation for ambiguous or sensitive issues.

• Ensure new systems and workflows are documented, supportable, measurable, and clearly owned after launch.

Security and Compliance:

• Partner with Information Security, Security Engineering, GRC, Internal Audit, Legal, and People to implement practical security controls across IT operations.

• Develop, maintain, and enforce IT policies, standards, procedures, and evidence required for effective governance and audit readiness.

• Support identity governance, access reviews, role-based access, SSO, SCIM, privileged access, service-account governance, endpoint security, vendor reviews, and remediation of identified risks.

• Ensure IT processes follow least privilege, separation of duties, reliable approvals, traceability, and appropriate independent verification.

• Contribute to security investigations, incident response, business continuity, disaster recovery, and operational resilience planning.

• Balance strong security and compliance controls with a practical employee experience and manageable operational processes.

Vendor and Budget Management:

• Manage vendor relationships, renewals, service reviews, contract inputs, licensing, procurement, implementation, and operational escalations for IT-managed services.

• Manage the IT budget, forecast demand, evaluate total cost of ownership, and ensure cost-effective use of resources.

• Identify opportunities to consolidate tools, improve utilization, reduce waste, and retire unnecessary services.

• Partner with Business Systems, Finance, Security, Legal, and functional leaders to clarify ownership when a platform spans multiple organizations.

Program and Cross-Functional Leadership:

• Lead complex IT programs from problem definition through planning, implementation, adoption, measurement, and operational handoff.

• Establish program governance, milestones, risks, dependencies, decision logs, launch readiness, rollback plans, and post-launch reviews.

• Represent IT priorities, risks, decisions, and tradeoffs in executive and cross-functional forums.

• Communicate clearly with employees, managers, executives, and technical partners about change, expected impact, and required action.

• Act as a trusted advisor on IT strategy, service quality, technology investment, operational risk, and business continuity.

Problem Resolution and Support:

• Act as a senior escalation point for critical or cross-functional IT issues, providing strategic guidance and coordinating recovery when business operations are at risk.

• Ensure high-quality, empathetic, and consistent user support across regions, offices, and time zones.

• Use service, asset, incident, and operational data to identify trends, recurring problems, and opportunities for improvement.

• Build durable solutions that reduce repeat incidents and avoid dependence on heroic individual effort.

What You Bring to the Table

• Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field; relevant equivalent experience will also be considered. A Master’s degree or relevant certifications such as ITIL, PMP, CISSP, or CISM is preferred.

• 10+ years of progressive experience in IT, systems administration, infrastructure, workplace technology, or a related discipline, including at least 3 years in a people-leadership role.

• Proven experience leading an IT support, systems engineering, workplace technology, or corporate IT function in a distributed or global organization.

• Proven expertise in IT infrastructure, identity and access management, endpoint management, SaaS administration, systems management, service delivery, and network or workplace technology operations.

• Strong knowledge of cloud technologies, enterprise applications, ITSM practices, automation, and IT governance frameworks.

• Experience with modern workplace technologies such as Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom, Okta, Jamf or comparable MDM, Jira or comparable ITSM platforms, and endpoint-security tools.

• Practical understanding of security, privacy, risk, audit, and compliance expectations, including ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, SOX, or comparable standards.

• Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, and inspire a high-performing distributed team.

• Experience managing budgets, vendors, renewals, licensing, procurement, technology contracts, and total cost of ownership.

• Experience delivering cross-functional programs, managing competing priorities, and establishing clear ownership and accountability.

• Exceptional problem-solving, decision-making, written, verbal, and executive communication skills.

• Strong judgment when balancing employee experience, operational efficiency, security, privacy, governance, and cost.

What We Offer

We have all the usual perks and benefits but what we can really offer you is a fantastic work environment powered by an amazing team.

• Industry competitive compensation and equity plan

• Flexible time off, sick days, and 13 paid holidays

• Comprehensive medical insurance including Health, Dental and Vision

• Paid parental leave (plus fertility, adoption and other family planning benefits)

• In-office workspace (San Francisco & Chicago)

• Monthly allowance for wellness, reading and access to LinkedIn Learning for continued development

• Events and activities both team-based and company wide that inspire, educate and cultivate

• The compensation range for this role is $166,700 to $232,000, based on experience.

Pantheon is an equal opportunity employer and we welcome applications from all backgrounds regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, disability, or any other classification protected by law. Pantheon complies with federal and local disability laws and makes reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation due to a disability for any part of the interview process, please contact talent@pantheon.io. Pursuant to local and federal regulations, Pantheon will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records for employment.

After an offer is made and accepted, E-verify will be utilized to establish your identity and employment eligibility as required by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.

Overview

Where Complexity Meets Structure and Top Performers Win

There is a reason enterprise buyers are moving to Paycor. We built something no one else in the market can replicate: AI-enabled enterprise technology backed by the deepest operational expertise in the HCM industry. Our platform is purpose-built for how enterprise HR and finance actually work. When you sell for Paycor, you are not asking buyers to take a leap of faith. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineering, Propulsion
jobs.description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and capital-efficient approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to support a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and supporting a growing space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to design, build, and operate its own spacecraft in orbit. Next, Haven-1 is targeted to become the world’s first commercial space station, with launch anticipated in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced two new offerings leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo: Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line; and Vast Lunar Systems, power, communications, and habitats for the Moon.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities capable of manufacturing America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for Mars, dedicated modules for government partners, and other crewed systems designed to unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast is looking for a Manufacturing Engineer, Propulsion, reporting to the Lead Manufacturing Engineer, Propulsion, to own components and subassemblies and support the development, production, and integration of propulsion and pressurization hardware for artificial-gravity human-rated space stations.

This will be a full-time, exempt position located in our Long Beach location.

Responsibilities

• Support the propulsion manufacturing engineering team day to day: execute against priorities set by the Lead, communicate status and blockers, and share knowledge with peers

• Contribute to team onboarding and knowledge sharing; at E3, informally mentor newer engineers

• Own manufacturing development, production readiness, and build execution for assigned propulsion and pressurization hardware (typically 1-2 components or subassemblies), including valves, regulators, tubing, ducting, manifolds, COPVs, fittings, and instrumentation, working hands-on on the floor

• Support the propulsion manufacturing schedule and build sequencing across development, qualification, and flight builds for owned hardware

• Report hardware status, risks, and mitigation plans for owned hardware to the Lead and cross-functional partners

• Partner with propulsion and systems design teams to drive design for manufacturing and manufacturing readiness

• Develop, qualify, and optimize manufacturing processes and production equipment with increasing independence by level, including welding, brazing, tube fabrication, precision cleaning, and proof and leak testing

• Work with suppliers on manufacturing readiness, including review of supplier processes and documentation

• Partner with quality engineering to define inspection methods, acceptance criteria, and process controls for safety-critical fluid components

• Uphold a strong safety and quality culture for high-pressure and hazardous fluid hardware

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, manufacturing, or aerospace engineering, or a related discipline

• Manufacturing engineering experience in aerospace, propulsion, or high-reliability fluid systems (E1: 0-2 years; E2: 2-4 years; E3: 5+ years; internships and co-ops count toward E1)

• Hands-on hardware experience supporting fabrication, assembly, integration, and/or testing of fluid system hardware (internship, co-op, or project-based experience acceptable)

• Experience, or demonstrated ability to learn quickly, developing manufacturing processes, travelers, work instructions, and production documentation for safety-critical hardware

• Working knowledge of CAD tools (e.g., Siemens NX) with the ability to review designs, generate manufacturing documentation, and support assembly or test tooling design

• Ability to own a component, subassembly, or workstream and drive it to completion with increasing independence by level

• Willingness to work evenings and/or weekends as needed to support critical propulsion testing and mission milestones

Preferred Qualifications

• Master’s degree in an engineering discipline

• Experience leading a project or workstream, or mentoring interns or newer engineers

• Experience with manufacturing and assembly of high-pressure or hazardous fluid systems, including propellant feed, pressurization, venting, and purge systems

• Strong understanding of propulsion fluid system manufacturing, including tube fabrication, welding, brazing, precision cleaning, and assembly processes

• Hands-on experience testing, troubleshooting, and qualifying propulsion or fluid components, including proof, leak, and functional testing

• Experience integrating COPVs, valves, regulators, and instrumentation into flight systems

• Experience developing and qualifying production equipment, assembly tooling, and test tooling

• Strong GD&T knowledge and experience creating and reviewing engineering drawings

• Experience with Siemens NX

• Experience reviewing and approving supplier manufacturing processes and documentation

• Proven problem-solving skills with hands-on root cause analysis and corrective and preventive action experience

• Strong cross-functional communication skills and the ability to work effectively with propulsion, systems, test, and quality teams

• High attention to detail and a strong ownership mindset for safety-critical hardware

Pay Range:

• Manufacturing Engineer I, Propulsion: $86,100.00 - $122,220.00

• Manufacturing Engineer II, Propulsion: $112,340.00 - $159,468.00

• Senior Manufacturing Engineer, Propulsion: $137,760.00 - $195,552.00

We calibrate level and compensation to the selected candidate's experience and demonstrated capability. We welcome applicants across a range of experience levels to apply.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Base salary will vary depending on job-related knowledge, education, skills, experience, business needs, and market demand. Salary is just one component of our comprehensive compensation package. Full-time employees also receive company equity, as well as access to a full suite of compelling benefits and perks, including: medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents, generous paid time off; up to 20+ days of vacation for exempt staff and up to 10+ days of vacation for non-exempt staff with the ability to cash-out unused vacation annually, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, ClassPass credits, personalized mental healthcare through Spring Health, and other discounts and perks. We also take pride in offering exceptional food perks, with snacks, drip coffee & onsite barista, cold drinks, and dinner meals remaining free of charge, and lunch subsidized as part of Vast’s ongoing commitment to providing high-quality meals for employees.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Vast is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Vast is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES
